6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.P1Points
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.SectionsBaseChange
8	
9	/-!
10	# The canonical section of `ℙ¹` over an arbitrary test ring
11	
12	`ℙ¹` has a canonical rational point — the origin `[1 : 0]` of the first standard chart — and
13	that point exists over *every* base, not only over a separably closed field.  This file packages
14	it as a **section functor**: for every commutative `k`-algebra `A` a morphism
15	
16	  `P1.overSection k A : overSpec k A ⟶ (P1.asOver k)`
17	
18	in `Over (Spec k)`, natural in `A` (`P1.overSection_naturality`).  It is `[1 : 0]` through the
19	chart `D₊(X₀)`, built from `P1Points.fromSpecChart` with the constant chart coordinate `0`; the
20	over-`k` condition is `fromSpecChart_structureMap`.
21	
22	## Why this is worth a file
23	
24	The representability route reaches `ℙ¹` through
25	`AlgebraicGeometry.jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton` and the section-conditional
26	étale↔Zariski comparison
27	`AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section` / `relPicToPicEt_surjective_of_section`
28	(`Picard/EffectivityClose.lean`, `Picard/PicEtUnitFieldComparison.lean`).  Both of those
29	consume a section `σ : overSpec k _ ⟶ C` of the curve.  The inbox pricing `I-1603` records that
30	this input — "a `k`-rational point at `ℙ¹`" — **is not constructed anywhere in this project**,
31	even though `ℙ¹` has one over any ring.  This file constructs it, unconditionally on the base
32	field and over an arbitrary test ring, so the comparison lemmas can be instantiated at `ℙ¹`.
33	
34	Nothing here is new mathematics: it is the origin of a chart.  The value is that the section a
35	dozen downstream lemmas assume as a hypothesis now exists as a term, at the object the headline
36	is about.
37	-/
38	
39	set_option autoImplicit false
40	
41	universe u
42	
43	open CategoryTheory MonoidalCategory
44	
45	open scoped CartesianMonoidalCategory
46	
47	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
48	
49	namespace P1
50	
51	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
52	
53	/-- The canonical `A`-point `[1 : 0]` of `ℙ¹`, as a morphism `Spec A ⟶ ℙ¹` over `k`.
54	
55	It is `fromSpecChart` through the first chart `D₊(X₀)` with chart coordinate `0`, i.e. the origin
56	of that chart.  Being through a chart it is defined for every ring, with no positivity,
57	separable-closure or nonemptiness hypothesis. -/
58	noncomputable def specPoint : Spec (.of A) ⟶ P1 k :=
59	  fromSpecChart k (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)) 0 (0 : A)
60	
61	/-- `specPoint` is a morphism over `k`: composing with the structure map of `ℙ¹` gives the
62	structure map `Spec A ⟶ Spec k` of `overSpec k A`. -/
63	theorem specPoint_structureMap :
64	    specPoint k A ≫ structureMap k = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)) := by
65	  rw [specPoint, fromSpecChart_structureMap]
66	
67	/-- **The canonical section of `ℙ¹` over the test ring `A`**: `[1 : 0]` as a morphism
68	`overSpec k A ⟶ (P1.asOver k)` in `Over (Spec k)`.
69	
70	This is the section `σ` that `PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section`, `relPicToPicEt_surjective_of_section`
71	and the challenge-target chain all take as a hypothesis; it exists at every test ring. -/
72	noncomputable def overSection : overSpec k A ⟶ (P1.asOver k) :=
73	  Over.homMk (specPoint k A) (specPoint_structureMap k A)
74	
75	@[simp]
76	theorem overSection_left : (overSection k A).left = specPoint k A := rfl
77	
78	/-! ## The global `k`-rational point
79	
80	The monoidal unit `𝟙_ (Over (Spec k))` is definitionally `Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec k)) = overSpec k k`
81	(the base changed along `𝟙 : k → k`), so the section at the test ring `A = k` is a **global
82	`k`-rational point** `𝟙_ ⟶ (P1.asOver k)`.  This is the `P : 𝟙_ ⟶ P1.asOver k` that
83	`Curve/P1H1Vanishing.lean` and the challenge target `exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` record as
84	constructed nowhere in the project. -/
85	
86	/-- **The global `k`-rational point of `ℙ¹`**: the origin `[1 : 0]`, as a morphism from the
87	monoidal unit of `Over (Spec k)`.  This is the point hypothesis `P` of the challenge's
88	`JacobianData.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` at `ℙ¹`. -/
89	noncomputable def unitPoint : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ (P1.asOver k) :=
90	  Over.homMk (specPoint k k) (by
91	    change specPoint k k ≫ structureMap k = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
92	    rw [specPoint_structureMap,
93	      show (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k)) = 𝟙 (CommRingCat.of k) from by ext x; simp,
94	      Spec.map_id])
95	
96	@[simp]
97	theorem unitPoint_left : (unitPoint k).left = specPoint k k := rfl
98	
99	/-! ## Naturality
100	
101	The point `[1 : 0]` is *constant*: it does not depend on the test ring, only on `ℙ¹`.  So
102	base-changing the section along an algebra map `A → B` lands on the section at `B`.  Stated at
103	the scheme level (`specPoint_naturality`) it needs no `Over`-category machinery, so this file
104	stays below the Picard layer that owns `Over.overSpecMap`. -/
105	
106	variable (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
107	
108	/-- **Naturality of the canonical point** at the scheme level: pulling `specPoint` back along
109	`Spec` of the algebra map `A → B` is `specPoint` at `B`.
110	
111	`fromSpecChart` is natural in the ring (`SpecMap_fromSpecChart`), and the chart coordinate is the
112	constant `0`, which the algebra map sends to `0`; the base map `k → B` factors as `k → A → B` by
113	the scalar tower. -/
114	theorem specPoint_naturality (φ : A →ₐ[k] B) :
115	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom) ≫ specPoint k A = specPoint k B := by
116	  rw [specPoint, specPoint, SpecMap_fromSpecChart]
117	  congr 1
118	  · rw [← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
119	    congr 1
120	    exact φ.comp_algebraMap
121	  · exact map_zero _
122	
123	end P1
124	
125	end AlgebraicGeometry
